As he reached Lolici and saw them there, he was so afraid that he fled because he was so afraid of them as if they were still alive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Sellers, shall we close the -- this issue here?

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am satisfied.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: So am I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And also because I understand a little bit of the language and I do recall having heard him mention the name Azem. No, it's not transcript, but now we have the explanation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SELLERS
utterances.text: Absolutely fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I found your intervention very pertinent and very legitimate to start with. Yes, Ms. Vidovic, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wish to thank Madam Sellers. Could this document please be assigned a number. I'm not sure about the last one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No, we haven't assigned a number to it as of yet. This document, which consists of two pages with ERN 04359361, one in B/C/S and one in English, being the direct translation thereof, is being marked as Defence Exhibit D914.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the usher please show the witness another document, which is issued by the Bratunac Brigade dated 2nd January, 1993, bearing the number 04359310, and the title is "the list of women volunteers who volunteered on the 15th of May, 1992, to provide help to the Army of Republika Srpska, that is the Bratunac Brigade."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at the document. The list starts with the platoon commander, Vladanka Petrovic, and later there are 26 more names. The text below the list states: "Commander of the women's platoon, Vladanka Petrovic, handed over her duty of platoon commander to Janja Ostojic who was deployed in this brigade and has been there since 15 May, 1992. Vladanka Petrovic assumes another duty to meet the needs and obligations of the brigade." Witness, please look at the list first and tell us whether you recognise any of the persons listed herein. Please look at the name under number 3, Nada Milanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this person hails from Kravica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at number 17, Slavica Kojic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Slavica Kojic is from Kajici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Kajici also a hamlet of Kravica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Do you find it unusual that the Serb army should have had women as its members? Do you find that unusual?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing was unusual to us. We knew that whoever was able-bodied, even those of an advanced age, were members of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I will move to a different topic now. After the attack on the 29th of May, 1992, did the attacks on Konjevic Polje cease in the course of the summer of 1992 or did they go on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, the attacks on Konjevic Polje continued. They were fiercer and fiercer every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Vidovic, we haven't given a number to the last document you used, and this document, which consists of two pages, one --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One in B/C/S and the other one in English with ERN 04359310 is being tendered and marked as Defence Exhibit D915.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I was talking about the attacks for which you stated that they continued throughout the summer. Where did these attacks come from most often?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether in the course of the summer of 1992 you saw any other artillery positions, if any, in the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. There was a Howitzer and an anti-aircraft machine-gun at Gornji Bacici. There was a mortar there also next to the barn. In Banjevici there was a mortar as well as in Obackici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to know about these positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One could see them with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you described for us a number of mortar and artillery positions. These pieces, were they positioned within the Serb villages that you mentioned themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were positioned some 20 metres away from the houses, not more than that, next to the villages themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you describe for the Trial Chamber the position of weapons in Siljkovici, the battery in Siljkovici, where was it exactly deployed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was right next to the village, about 20 metres away from the houses.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe in more detail the location of artillery pieces in Gornji Bacici that you also stated to have seen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Gornji Bacici there was a hillock next to a barn where a

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please do your best in avoiding to mention your village, your home, and I will do the same on my part in putting questions to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could we go into private session for a while?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And I think sometimes when you're dealing with these it's better to go and stay in private session for the entire duration of the series of questions dealing with particular events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, we are in open session. Now we'll have another break which requires at least 30 minutes because of the redactions. Yep. I'm sorry about this, Madam Vidovic and Mr. Wubben, but unfortunately I can't avoid it any further. So we'll have a 30-minute break and then we'll have the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the usher to put another document before the witness. This is the list of persons from military post 2465/5 paid for official troop trip and fee as well as pay for June 1992. The document is from number 01335316 to 01335337.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the list in front of you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you confirm the following. Is the document entitled "Kravica," the title itself on the first page? Can you see that? In the left corner --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I didn't hear your reply.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
